It is used as a screening tool to categorize individuals into weight status categories: underweight, normal weight, overweight, and obese. The formula is weight in kilograms divided by the square of height in meters."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "How is BMI calculated?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "BMI is calculated using the formula: BMI = weight (kg) / height (m) squared. In imperial units, the formula is: BMI = (weight in lbs x 703) / height in inches squared. The multiplication factor of 703 converts the imperial measurements to align with the metric-based BMI scale."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "What is a healthy BMI?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "For most adults, a healthy BMI falls between 18.5 and 24.9. A BMI below 18.5 is classified as underweight, 25 to 29.9 is overweight, and 30 or above is obese. These ranges may differ for certain ethnic groups and age brackets."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Is BMI different for children?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "Yes. For children and teens aged 2-19, BMI is interpreted using age- and sex-specific percentiles rather than the fixed adult cutoffs. A child at the 85th to 94th percentile is considered overweight, and at or above the 95th percentile is considered obese."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Is BMI accurate for athletes?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "BMI may overestimate body fat in athletes and others with muscular builds because it cannot distinguish between muscle mass and fat mass. Athletes with high muscle mass may have a high BMI but low body fat percentage. Body fat percentage or DEXA scans provide more accurate assessments for athletic individuals."}}, {"@type": "Question", "name": "Does BMI differ by ethnicity?", "acceptedAnswer": {"@type": "Answer", "text": "Yes. Research has shown that BMI health risks vary across ethnic groups. For example, Asian populations may have higher health risks at lower BMI values, which is why some countries use a cutoff of 23 (rather than 25) for overweight. The WHO has acknowledged these differences in its guidelines."}} ] } ] } </script>
